actors.name: Driver caller
actors.description: Application or middleware code that calls the driver and supplies the configuration structure.

actors.name: Safety Supervisor middleware
actors.description: Middleware in examples/safety-supervisor that uses this driver (CON-IWDG-006).

actors.name: IWDG peripheral
actors.description: The independent watchdog hardware of the STM32N657X0 that the driver controls and that the driver waits on.

use_cases.title: Configure and start the watchdog
use_cases.goal: Apply a caller-supplied configuration (timeout setting, and the optional window and early-wakeup settings) to the watchdog and start it, without ever offering a way to stop it. Software watchdog mode only (CON-IWDG-007); starting an already running watchdog changes nothing and returns an already-running status. Before the first load request the start service waits, bounded by the caller timeout, until every register-update flag is clear; no other settling delay is required (CON-IWDG-010). The start service checks its arguments first; an invalid argument returns invalid-parameter even when the watchdog is already running (CON-IWDG-014). With valid arguments it writes the prescaler, reload, window and early-wakeup settings, waits until every register-update flag is clear and returns success; it issues no extra load request after the window write and does not confirm that a reload took effect (CON-IWDG-015).

use_cases.title: Refresh the watchdog
use_cases.goal: Reload the watchdog counter in time so that the watchdog does not reset the device while the software is healthy. The service issues the request and returns; it does not detect a refresh the hardware ignored (CON-IWDG-008). The caller refreshes only through this service and keeps its refresh timing clear of the window; the driver neither reports nor guards the reloads a configuration write causes, and this caller duty is stated in the driver interface (CON-IWDG-011).

use_cases.title: Configure the optional window
use_cases.goal: Optionally set a window so that a refresh outside the permitted period is treated as a fault by the hardware. The window is configured only by the start service, before the first refresh, and never changed while the watchdog runs (CON-IWDG-010). The driver accepts every window value the register allows; keeping the first and later refreshes inside the window is the caller's duty (CON-IWDG-015, CON-IWDG-011).

use_cases.title: Configure the early-wakeup interrupt
use_cases.goal: Enable and configure the early-wakeup interrupt and clear its pending flag, so the caller is warned before the watchdog expires. The early-wakeup value is a field of the start configuration; there is no separate early-wakeup configuration service (CON-IWDG-013, replacing that part of CON-IWDG-002). The interrupt is configured only by the start service, before the first refresh, and never changed while the watchdog runs (CON-IWDG-010).

use_cases.title: Query pending register updates
use_cases.goal: Let the caller ask whether a prescaler, reload, window or early-wakeup update is still pending in the hardware, without blocking.

use_cases.title: Read the IWDG reset cause
use_cases.goal: Let the caller read the reset cause flag set by the IWDG after a restart, to decide whether the last reset was a watchdog reset.

use_cases.title: Bounded waiting and no stop
use_cases.goal: Every wait for the hardware ends within a caller-supplied timeout of 1 to 1000 ms (1 ms tick) with a reported timeout status, and no driver service stops a started watchdog (CON-IWDG-003, -004, -009). A timeout outside 1 to 1000 ms makes the service return an invalid-parameter status without accessing the hardware (CON-IWDG-012). Every service checks its arguments first, so an invalid argument returns invalid-parameter even when the watchdog is already running (CON-IWDG-014).

use_cases.title: Use of the driver by the Safety Supervisor
use_cases.goal: Provide driver interface requirements the Safety Supervisor software requirements can link to as interfaces.

out_of_scope.reason: Debug freeze behaviour is not in the list of driver services of CON-IWDG-002.

assumptions.text: CON-IWDG-001 to CON-IWDG-015 in scope.md (task constraints and product decisions) are the only stakeholder needs; no separate STK needs exist, so use cases leave needs empty and rely on document sections.

Per CON-IWDG-007 the product uses the software watchdog mode; hardware watchdog mode (running from power-on) is out of scope for the driver, and the start service called on a running watchdog changes nothing and returns an already-running status.

Per CON-IWDG-008 the driver does not detect a refresh the hardware ignored; the refresh service issues the request and returns, and no separate status exists for it. Such a fault is caught by the caller's own supervision.
Per CON-IWDG-009 every bounded wait takes a caller-supplied timeout of 1 to 1000 ms, measured with the platform 1 ms tick, and returns a timeout status when it has elapsed unfinished.

Per CON-IWDG-010 the window option and the early-wakeup interrupt are configured only by the start service, before the first refresh, and never while the watchdog runs; before the first load request the start service waits until every register-update flag is clear, bounded by the caller timeout, and no other settling delay is required.

Per CON-IWDG-011 the driver neither reports nor guards the reloads a configuration write causes; the caller refreshes only through the refresh service and keeps its refresh timing clear of the window, a duty stated in the driver interface.
Per CON-IWDG-012 a timeout outside 1 to 1000 ms yields an invalid-parameter status without any hardware access.
Per CON-IWDG-013 the early-wakeup value is a field of the start configuration and no separate early-wakeup configuration service exists; this replaces that part of CON-IWDG-002.

Per CON-IWDG-014 every service checks its arguments first; an invalid argument returns invalid-parameter even when the watchdog is already running, and the already-running status applies only to a start call with valid arguments.

Per CON-IWDG-015 the start service writes prescaler, reload, window and early-wakeup settings, waits until every register-update flag is clear and returns success, with no extra load request after the window write and no confirmation that a reload took effect; every register-allowed window value is accepted and refresh timing inside the window is the caller's duty.
Only chapter 59 of RM0486 is in the document scope, except for the reset cause flag, whose location is an open point.
Driver requirements are written at the level set in the project's requirement_style; no hardware fact is stated without a section and page of RM0486.

open_points.text: The reset cause flag set by the IWDG (UC-IWDG-006) is not described in the IWDG chapter; the chapter and page that describe it have not yet been identified in the outline.
The inputs do not say how the driver must behave when the device enters a low power mode while the watchdog runs; only the manual section is known.
